slides.title: Master of Management (Human Resources)
slides.subtitle: Durability assessment against the 2026 handbook — and the session in which you correct it

slides.kicker: Why you are in this room
slides.statement: We scored this program using only what the handbook documents, with one rater, on a draft instrument. We have already corrected this report twice. I am not here to defend the numbers — I am here to find out which of them are wrong, what evidence we could not see, and where the instrument itself measures the wrong thing.
slides.attribution: If you leave without having changed something, we have run this badly.

slides.title: What Evidura is
slides.subtitle: Evidura is the platform · the Durability Rating is the signal · DFVA is the method underneath

left.heading: What it is
items: An assessment of what a curriculum documents that it teaches and assesses
Two independent coordinates: where graduates go, and what the curriculum builds
Anchored on the TEQSA adaptive capabilities and the HESF learning-outcome clauses
Fully quoted — every score cites handbook text verbatim, so any score can be overturned

right.heading: What it is not
items: Not a ranking — no program is compared with another here
Not a compliance instrument — not TEQSA, not AHRI, not an audit
Not a judgement of teaching quality — undocumented excellence scores low, and we say so
Not a rating you have been given — no position label is reported for this program

slides.title: Two coordinates, never one number
slides.subtitle: A single total would hide which problem you have

bullets.text: Computed from this program's own alumni destination record against a published occupational exposure index. A property of the occupations graduates enter. Nobody in this room controls it.
C1–C5, the TEQSA adaptive capabilities: distributed cognition, evaluative judgement, AI literacy and governance, transfer, inquiry. Entirely within the program's control.
W1–W3, added 2026-08-14: professional communication and conduct, authentic task design, work-situated learning. Reported beside adaptiveness and never added to it.

slides.note: A program strong on workplace practice and weak on adaptiveness has a different problem from the reverse.

slides.title: The four rules that decide arguments
slides.subtitle: Most objections to a score are really objections to one of these

bullets.text: Anchors state what evidence must exist, not how good it is. So two raters reading the same page reach the same score.
A stated learning outcome caps an item at level 1. Stated graduate attributes are not evidence of attainment (Barrie 2006).
Every score quotes its source, so any score can be checked — and overturned — by anyone in this room.
Scored from what the task requires, never from the word 'authentic'. The label has become a thought-terminating cliché (Fawns et al. 2024).

slides.note: And one convention: where evidence straddles two levels, the lower level is awarded and the straddle is recorded. Seven were recorded here.

slides.title: How this report was made
slides.subtitle: Provenance, in full — including what has not been done
rows: 35 handbook pages captured 2026-08-14 on a paced browser queue: course overview, attributes, structure, and the overview + assessment pages of all 11 compulsory subjects and 5 selectives.
The program's own exact-name JIR/LiveAlumni record — 28 graduates, 15 destination titles, crosswalked to the published Felten exposure index.
Named regulatory instruments and reported survey data. No job-advertisement platform was sampled.
One rater on the v4.1 draft anchors, with an adversarial pass over every level-3 score and gate.
No content-validity panel. No inter-rater reliability study. No external review of the W items at all.
slides.note: The instrument's own limitations are printed in the report, not discovered in the room.

slides.statement: An earlier version said this program had no alumni record — wrong file checked. And an earlier version was scored on 22 of the 35 pages, because a capture agent used 'failed' to mean 'deprioritised'. We recaptured and re-scored. Two items changed, and both went down.
slides.attribution: Which matters for today: when you tell us we have missed something, the correction does not reliably go up.

slides.title: The scorecard
slides.subtitle: Panel C v4.1 · scored from documented curriculum evidence
slides.railNote: Reported side by side. Never added. No position label until v4 medians exist.
slides.note: G1 passes on the accredited compulsory sequence — 137.5 of 200 credit points, AHRI-accredited and SHRM-aligned.

findings.heading: The destination set is the finding
findings.text: Eleven of fifteen titles sit between 95 and 96. No low-exposure tail. A property of the occupations, not a judgement of the program.

findings.heading: C3 = 1/3 — AI is a stated outcome, assessed nowhere compulsory
findings.text: MGMT90267 is an elective. Meanwhile three regulatory instruments put governance of automated employment decisions on HR — one Australian and in force.

findings.heading: C2 and C4 both stop one step short, on the same evidence
findings.text: MGMT90140 documents the diagnosis but not the plan. Two items move on one documentation change — if the subject already asks for it. Does it?

findings.heading: The workplace provision is real, and optional
findings.text: BUSA90473 is level-3 material sitting in a selective slot. A student can finish the 200-point program without entering a workplace.

slides.title: Where graduates go
slides.subtitle: Exact-name alumni record, n = 28 · exposure via the published Felten index, rescaled 0–100
rows: Human Resources Administrator · Assistant · Recruitment Administrator
HR Advisor · HR Officer · People and Culture Advisor
slides.note: Screening, scheduling, records administration, first-pass matching and policy drafting are the tasks that define these occupations — and the tasks current systems already do.

slides.subtitle: Nothing is re-scored in the room. Everything you supply is re-scored against the evidence afterwards, and the change is published.

slides.title: What happens to what you say today

items.text: Re-captured where needed and re-scored against the new evidence. Republished with a dated correction note naming what changed — the same treatment the two existing corrections got.
Recorded as a rater-disagreement case for the inter-rater reliability study. Disagreement about whether a line satisfies an anchor is a finding there, not noise.
Routed to the Panel C decision log and the content-validity panel that has not yet run.

slides.footerNote: Every disputed item is either re-scored against supplied evidence or answered in writing with the reason it stands. Nothing is left as 'noted'.
